description: Safe, read-only-behavior code-quality deep dive across the EXISTING pipeline modules (tools/*.py, excluding the new Task 1 files). Apply only SAFE, behavior-preserving fixes; record everything else found as a recommendation. Independent of FEAT-001 (touches a disjoint set of files: existing tools/*.py modules and tests only, never tools/post_comments_runner.py, tools/web/post_comments_controller.py, or the Task 1 UI/route additions) -- ordered second here only to keep the higher-risk feature's review cycle isolated first.
steps: Re-read .agents/tasks/ooj-audit-findings.md and .agents/tasks/rollback-plan.md in full before changing anything, to build the do-not-re-flag list: do NOT re-propose P1-1/P1-2/P1-3/P1-5 as new findings (already catalogued, several explicitly marked BEHAVIOR-CHANGING -- leave alone), do NOT re-enable apply_remarks.COLUMNS_TO_REMOVE, do NOT touch the SCC '>1000' checkbox always-tick-best-effort behavior, chunk sizes (SCC_UI_CHUNK/AUTO_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD/SCC_CHUNK_ATTEMPTS), the 45-minute-equivalent SCC_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_S-or-equivalent literal, or the no-heartbeat/no-auth-gate GCRS behavior described as intentionally reverted in rollback-plan.md.

tools/gcrs_mcscli.py: review _resolve_batch_with_edge_retry (and its use of EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS/EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_BACKOFF_S) for correctness against its own docstring contract (on the Edge transport, retry a TransportError up to EDGE_BATCH_RETRY_ATTEMPTS times with the given backoff, then return the chunk's TIDs as errored instead of raising; on any non-Edge transport call _resolve once with no retry). Read the current implementation carefully -- note it already does NOT use a separate _is_failed_to_fetch filter (unlike the version described in rollback-plan.md section 2.2); it retries ANY TransportError on Edge. Confirm this matches the live code's actual docstring and is not a bug; if the broader retry-on-any-TransportError (vs rollback-plan's narrower 'Failed to fetch'-only filter) looks like an unintentional behavior drift, do NOT silently narrow it -- it is a separate, already-landed design (2026-10-04 per Docs/changes.md) distinct from the Oct-8 rollback-plan.md draft; leave it as-is and only note the observation in the findings report, do not change retry-filtering behavior.

tools/gcrs_mcscli.py: check tests/test_polygon_workflow.py (and any other tests/test_*.py) for existing coverage of _resolve_batch_with_edge_retry's three branches (success-first-try, retry-then-succeed, retry-exhausted-degrades-and-caller-continues-to-next-batch via fetch()'s batch_errored list). If any of these three branches is genuinely untested, add OFFLINE tests to a new or existing non-Task-1 test file (e.g. a new tests/test_gcrs_retry.py, following tests/test_scc_retry.py's unittest.mock.patch.object fake-session style) using a fake FailoverSiwSession-like object with a controllable transport_name and a _resolve stub that raises TransportError N times then succeeds (or always raises). Do NOT change gcrs_mcscli.py's logic unless a genuine bug is found during this review; if one is found, fix it minimally and explain the fix in the findings report.

tools/gcrs_mcscli.py: delete the dead constant flagged as P3-1 in ooj-audit-findings.md if it is still present (`BATCH = 500`, unreferenced by _batch_size_for which only reads BATCH_MCSCLI/BATCH_EDGE) -- confirm it is truly unreferenced via a repo-wide search before deleting, then remove just that one line. This is explicitly marked SAFE in the audit.

tools/scc_client.py: verify the same-page re-search retry (_export_chunk_with_retry, _wait_for_download_or_notfound) is fully consistent -- confirm there is no leftover page.reload()/page.goto() call anywhere in the retry path (tests/test_scc_retry.py already asserts this for _export_chunk_with_retry; extend the same scrutiny to _wait_for_download_or_notfound and _goto_search's own retry-on-redirect path inside _export_small, which legitimately navigates for a DIFFERENT reason -- an auth redirect, not a chunk retry -- so leave _export_small's navigation alone and do not conflate it with the #C5 chunk-retry fix). Check every docstring/comment in scc_client.py for stale wording that still describes a page.reload()/goto()-based retry (e.g. verify _wait_for_download_or_notfound's and _export_chunk_with_retry's docstrings match current no-reload behavior -- read during planning and already appear consistent; re-confirm at implementation time and fix minimally if any stale sentence is found) -- also note the discrepancy between scc_client.py's live inline comment (_browser_export_chunk's docstring and _ensure_large_mode_checkbox's call site -- in the current file this is called unconditionally without raising on failure, consistent with rollback-plan.md's intended 'always-tick-best-effort' behavior) and leave that exact behavior untouched per the explicit instruction not to re-revert it.

tools/scc_client.py: do NOT change SCC_UI_CHUNK, AUTO_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD, SCC_CHUNK_ATTEMPTS, or the >1000 checkbox always-tick-best-effort call in _browser_export_chunk. If any other retry path in scc_client.py (e.g. inside _export_small's HTTP-redirect retry, or _fetch_rows_resilient's bisection-on-rejected-batch retry) still performs a page.goto()/reload() as part of recovering from a transient failure (as opposed to a legitimate one-time auth redirect), flag it in the findings report with a one-line recommendation; only change it if it is unambiguously the SAME class of chunk-retry-after-transient-UI-failure that #C5 already fixed elsewhere (do not touch _export_small's auth-redirect goto, which is a different, legitimate case).

Across tools/*.py generally (excluding the new Task 1 files): scan for (a) resource leaks -- Playwright contexts/pages/files opened without a guaranteed close on an exception path (e.g. check scc_client.fetch()'s try/finally around context.close()/cdp.detach(), gcrs_mcscli.fetch()'s try/finally around active_session.close(), and any other *_client.py/*_export.py/*_run.py module's browser-context lifecycle) -- fix only genuine leaks (an exception path that skips a close()) with a minimal try/finally, do not restructure working context managers; (b) overly broad `except Exception` that silently swallows a real bug instead of logging it -- grep for bare `except Exception:` / `except Exception as exc:` blocks with no log call in their body across tools/*.py and classify each as either an intentional 'never let X crash the pipeline' guard (already documented inline, e.g. server.py's _sanitize/_auto_setup wrappers, sanitize_captures.py's _unlink) which must be left alone, or a genuinely silent swallow with no logging -- add a minimal log(...) call (reusing whatever log callable is already in scope) to any genuinely silent one found, without changing control flow; (c) duplicated TID-normalization logic -- re-read ooj-audit-findings.md P1-4 (flagged as BEHAVIOR-CHANGING, explicitly NOT marked safe) and leave normalize_tid/_normalize_tid duplication alone unless a SAFE, non-behavior-changing extraction is possible (e.g. only if an identical, byte-for-byte duplicate function body exists in two modules with provably identical semantics on all inputs including DOC-case and '.0'-suffix handling -- given the audit explicitly found scc_client's version differs in DOC-case handling from gcrs_mcscli's, this duplication is NOT safely extractable without a behavior decision; do not extract it, only note in the findings report that it remains intentionally un-extracted per P1-4); (d) hardcoded paths that should go through tools/ooj_paths.py -- re-read ooj-audit-findings.md P0-1 (also marked a real, SAFE-to-fix finding: 'Centralize the Edge profile path... used by run_daily, scc_client, pnama_export, siw_client') -- check tools/run_daily.py's preflight(), tools/pnama_export.py's PROFILE_DIR, and tools/siw_client.py's EDGE_PROFILE-equivalent constant: if ooj_paths.EDGE_PROFILE already exists and these modules already import from it (tools/scc_client.py already does, confirmed during planning: `from ooj_paths import EDGE_PROFILE`), check whether run_daily.py/pnama_export.py/siw_client.py still have their OWN hardcoded copy of the same path literal instead of importing EDGE_PROFILE -- if so, this is the one SAFE fix explicitly called out in the audit's top shortlist (#4): switch each remaining hardcoded literal to `from ooj_paths import EDGE_PROFILE` with no other change, since ooj_paths.py already defines the identical default value and is override-compatible via OOJ_EDGE_PROFILE; (e) missing/stale docstrings or comments that no longer match the code, especially in files touched by recent manual hot-fixes (scc_client.py, gcrs_mcscli.py per Docs/changes.md's 2026-10-04/2026-10-08-dated entries) -- fix only clear, factual staleness (a comment describing removed behavior, a docstring citing a wrong constant name), not stylistic rewrites.

For every SAFE fix actually applied in the steps above, run `py -3.13 -m pytest tests -q` immediately after each file's edit (not batched at the end) and confirm the pass count stays at or above the current baseline with 0 failures, fixing forward before moving to the next file. Do not touch any existing test file's assertions to make a change 'pass' -- if a change breaks an existing test, the change is not actually behavior-preserving; revert that specific edit and record it as a NOT-applied finding instead.

Write c:\Users\kabideba\Desktop\Kiro OOJ Automation\.agents\tasks\py-deep-dive-findings.md: a short report with two sections -- 'Fixed (safe, applied)' listing each change made (file, one-line description, which test(s) cover/re-verify it) and 'Found but intentionally not changed' listing each item considered but left alone because it would alter behavior, with a one-line recommendation and a reference to the relevant ooj-audit-findings.md section where applicable (e.g. 'P1-4 TID normalization duplication -- left alone, see ooj-audit-findings.md').
acceptance_criteria: `py -3.13 -m pytest tests -q` passes with at least the pre-change baseline count (69) plus any new offline tests added for the GCRS retry branches, 0 failed, after every edit in this feature.

No change alters SCC's >1000-checkbox always-tick-best-effort behavior, SCC_UI_CHUNK/AUTO_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD/SCC_CHUNK_ATTEMPTS values, the SCC download timeout literal, or GCRS's current (non-rollback) retry-on-any-TransportError behavior.
No existing test file's assertions were weakened or rewritten to accommodate a change.
.agents/tasks/py-deep-dive-findings.md exists and lists every applied fix and every intentionally-not-changed finding with a one-line recommendation each.
verification: py -3.13 -m pytest tests -q   (from workspace root, run after each file edit; expect baseline-or-higher passed, 0 failed)

Manual review: diff each touched tools/*.py file against the steps above and confirm every change is either (a) a one-line safe fix explicitly itemized in the steps, or (b) a new offline test file with no production-code behavior change.
findings: Full report at .agents/tasks/py-deep-dive-findings.md. Baseline py -3.13 -m pytest tests -q = 77 passed, 0 failed; stayed at 77/0 after every edit. Fixed (safe, applied): tools/edge_preflight.py's PROFILE_DIR was still a standalone hardcoded literal identical to ooj_paths.EDGE_PROFILE's default (audit P0-1 / top shortlist #4) while run_daily.py/scc_client.py/pnama_export.py/siw_client.py already imported EDGE_PROFILE from ooj_paths -- switched edge_preflight.py to `from ooj_paths import EDGE_PROFILE` + `PROFILE_DIR = EDGE_PROFILE`, no other line changed; covered by tests/test_polygon_workflow.py::EdgePreflightTests plus the full suite. Found but intentionally not changed: gcrs_mcscli's retry-on-any-TransportError Edge batch retry matches its own docstring contract exactly and is a separate, already-landed 2026-10-04 design distinct from rollback-plan.md's narrower filter -- left as-is; all three of its branches (success-first-try, retry-then-succeed, retry-exhausted-degrades) already have offline tests in tests/test_polygon_workflow.py::FailurePathTests, so no new test file was needed. Audit P3-1's dead `BATCH = 500` constant is not present in the current gcrs_mcscli.py (already resolved). scc_client.py's chunk-retry path has no page.reload()/goto() anywhere (confirmed consistent with tests/test_scc_retry.py); _export_small's goto is a distinct, legitimate HTTP-redirect case and was left alone; the >1000-checkbox always-tick-best-effort call, SCC_UI_CHUNK/AUTO_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD/SCC_CHUNK_ATTEMPTS, and the 45*60 download timeout literal are all unchanged. No resource leaks found (every browser-context/session close is already in try/finally). No genuinely silent `except Exception` swallow found -- every instance is either a documented cleanup/best-effort guard or already logs. TID normalization duplication (P1-4) remains intentionally un-extracted (scc_client's DOC-case handling still differs from gcrs_mcscli/polygon_check) -- left alone per the audit. Docstring staleness items P4-4 ('six protected remarks') and P4-5 (_state_display comment) were already fixed in an earlier pass; no further stale wording found. No existing test assertions were weakened or rewritten.
